TMax-15K.reason: Emit a JSON phase plan covering every table exactly once under hard dependency constraints, minimising a provided simulator's latency below a numeric threshold. Same loop.
Bin packing under a capacity cap and a conflict constraint, scored on packing efficiency; must minimise bundle count against an oracle baseline.
Heuristic search (GA/annealing/hill climb) over a 4^15 space to beat a fitness threshold, because brute force will not finish. Same search-to-a-budget skill.
Choose one version per package satisfying all range constraints while minimising summed cost, writing the assignment as JSON. Constrained min-cost assignment.
Pack ordered tasks into sequential batches so no batch exceeds a cost cap; the same greedy-fill-with-a-cap decision as filling a shape bucket.
Minimise a total cost whose per-edge values only come from calling a provided cost oracle, and emit the plan as JSON. Same opaque-cost-model reasoning.
Iteratively refine the implementation until a scoring binary reports at least 95.0; identical measure-refine-remeasure loop against an external scorer.
Implement a plan cost estimator that walks a plan tree and sums per-operation base costs - reading and applying a cost model, as cost_model.py must be here.
Assignment where naive greedy fails because a tightly-constrained item's only option gets taken first; the same failure mode when shapes are scarce.
Subset-sum solver over candidate lengths to hit exact target durations; combinatorial fill of a fixed budget, which is padding minimisation in miniature.

notes: The shortlist was almost useless for this task: lexical retrieval latched onto 'inference', 'benchmark', 'batch' and '/app' boilerplate and surfaced ETL/tokenisation chores. Every strong TMax pick here came from my own searches for packing, constrained assignment, cost models and threshold-beating objectives - notably task_001798_23078e06, which is structurally the same task (plan file, every item once, hard constraints, provided simulator, numeric threshold). Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld have essentially no combinatorial-optimisation content; their tens are honest but weak (N-Queens and benchmark-versus-threshold chores are the best on offer). SWE-Smith's only real angle is dask's chunk-sizing and scheduler-optimisation code. SWE-Rebench is better than expected because pyomo/openmdao/smac3 put real constrained-optimisation machinery in scope, and transformers' data collator is the one genuine LLM-batching-and-padding entry in the whole pool.
